Haydon Hall, 110 Laurier Avenue West, Ottawa, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, beginning at 10:00 a.m. The Mayor, Mark Sutcliffe, presided over the meeting from Council Chambers with some Members attending in person and the remaining Members participating remotely by Zoom.

sub_agendas_items.title: Feasibility Review of Future Park Space

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS there is a desire from residents to create more park space and community gathering space in the central part of the Fernbank community, due to increasing development pressures; and
WHEREAS there is an existing open space owned by the City of Ottawa along the Trans Canada Trail immediately east of Robert Grant Avenue of approximately 3,800 square metres; and
WHEREAS this unaddressed parcel of land is not suitable for housing or other development; and
WHEREAS Village Square Park in Stittsville is located on a similar-sized piece of land along the Trans Canada Trail at Abbott Street; and
WHEREAS there is a surplus of funding in the Ward 6 Stittsville Cash In Lieu of Parkland account.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to review the feasibility of adapting this parcel of land as a future park space, identifying any constraints, required studies, and any other considerations and report back to Council in Q1 2027 with their findings.

agenda_items.title: Motions Requiring Suspension of the Rules of Procedure

sub_agendas_items.title: Recognition of the officers and crew of HMCS Ottawa for their service to Canada

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion as it is appropriate and relevant for Council to consider this motion at that time HMCS Ottawa is in attendance.
WHEREAS November 11 marked Remembrance Day, with Canadians honouring the courage, service and sacrifice of those who have served our country and recognizing the men and women who continue to serve in the Canadian Armed Forces; and
WHEREAS the Royal Canadian Navy plays an important role in protecting Canadian sovereignty, defending national interests and supporting international peace and security; and
WHEREAS His Majesty's Canadian Ship (HMCS) Ottawa, proudly named after Canada's capital, recently completed a four-month deployment under Operations HORIZON and LATITUDE and travelled approximately 25, 000 nautical miles; and
WHEREAS the officers and crew of HMCS Ottawa served in the Indo-Pacific region and northern waters, working alongside Canada's allies to strengthen maritime security and international cooperation; and
WHEREAS members of the Canadian Armed Forces and their families make significant sacrifices, including extended periods of separation, in service to our country; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa takes great pride in its namesake ship and the contributions of those who serve in the Royal Canadian Navy;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Ottawa City Council recognize and thank the officers and crew of HMCS Ottawa, under the command of Commander Justin Simmons, for their successful 2026 deployment and dedicated service to Canada; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Ottawa City Council express its sincere appreciation to all Canadian Armed Forces members and their families for their service, dedication and sacrifice; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Office of the City Clerk provide a copy of this motion to HMCS Ottawa on behalf of Ottawa City Council.

sub_agendas_items.title: Recognition of Veterans Through the City of Ottawa Tree Dedication Program

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion as Remembrance Day was yesterday, and it is appropriate and relevant for Council to consider this motion as it relates to the recognition and commemoration of Canadian veterans.
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa's Tree Dedication Program offers residents an opportunity to dedicate trees in City parks to commemorate individuals and community contributions; and
WHEREAS Personal Dedications recognize individuals, events and milestones of personal significance to applicants and their loved ones, and are recognized with a tree identification tag and, beginning in 2027, the option of a standardized plaque at the base of the tree; and
WHEREAS Community Dedications recognize milestones, events and accomplishments of significance to the public, honouring and preserving a community's collective memories through personalized plaques at the base of dedicated trees; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa has a longstanding tradition of honouring Canadian veterans, including through its Commemorative Street Naming for Veterans Program; and
WHEREAS commemorative trees and plaques provide a meaningful and lasting opportunity to recognize the service and sacrifice of Canadian veterans;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to amend the Tree Dedication Program to explicitly identify Canadian veterans as eligible for Community Dedications; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff utilize the City's existing vetting process for nominations, in conjunction with the City's commemorative naming policy, to review and verify eligibility requirements for veteran dedications.

sub_agendas_items.title: FCM Support Resolution - Councillor Laura Dudas

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended as an updated Council support resolution is required to ensure the City’s representation at upcoming FCM Board meetings.
WHEREAS the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) represents the interests of member municipalities on policy and program matters that fall within federal jurisdiction; and
WHEREAS in accordance with the FCM’s By-laws, the City of Ottawa is eligible to select a representative to serve on the Board of Directors, in addition to Councillor Tierney, who serves as FCM President; and
WHEREAS on April 30, 2026, Council appointed Councillor Laura Dudas as the City of Ottawa’s representative to FCM’s Board of Directors, and approved a Council support resolution expiring at the end of the 2022-2026 Council term; and
WHEREAS it is anticipated that Council will confirm the City’s FCM representative for the 2026-2030 Term of Council at its meeting of December 9, 2026, following the Nominating Committee process; and
WHEREAS in order for Councillor Dudas to participate in upcoming FCM board meetings in early December, the end date of her Council support resolution must be extended beyond the end of the term;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council approve that the appointment of Councillor Laura Dudas as the City of Ottawa’s representative to FCM’s Board of Directors be extended until the end of 2026, or until such time as Council provides a new support resolution as part of its Nominating Committee process; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the City of Ottawa continues to assume all costs associated with the Council-appointed representative attending FCM’s Board of Directors meetings, to be funded from the Council Administration budget.

sub_agendas_items.title: Waiver of CILP Requirement for the Proposed Development at 175 Terence Matthews Crescent

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion so that it can be considered before the end of this Term of Council.
WHEREAS the Kanata South Business Park was originally approved in the1980’s; and
WHEREAS there is currently a proposed development at 175 Terence MatthewsCrescent that would be exempt from Parkland Dedication, or Cash-in-lieu ofParkland (CILP), under Section 11 of the Parkland Dedication By-law if previousparkland dedication records were available; and
WHEREAS staff cannot currently confirm whether parkland dedication criteriawere met at that time or anytime prior to amalgamation; and
WHEREAS there is a proposed development at 175 Terence Matthews Crescentthat would be exempt from Parkland Dedication, or Cash-in-lieu of Parkland(CILP), under Section 11 of the Parkland Dedication By-law if a previouscontribution could be confirmed; and
WHEREAS staff have agreed to conduct a search through the archives todetermine whether sufficient evidence is available to support waiver; and
WHEREAS the proposed development will benefit the local economy and addmore jobs to the Kanata South Business Park.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council waive the CILP requirement for the proposed development at 175 Terence Matthews Crescent contingent on the archival search.

sub_agendas_items.title: Advocating for eliminating twice yearly time changes

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS, in 2026, the provincial governments of British Columbia, Alberta and Manitoba as well as the territorial government of the Northwest Territories have all discontinued or are in the process of discontinuing the practice of switching between daylight and standard time; and,
WHEREAS the government of Saskatchewan in 1966 and the government of the Yukon in 2020 have implemented similar changes; and
WHEREAS the newly formed provincial government of Québec has also recently announced its intent to discontinue the practice of switching between daylight and standard time in that province; and,
WHEREAS, if the province of Québec implements this change, there are concerns of significant Impacts to residents of the National Capital Region, many of whom regularly cross the provincial boarder between Ontario and Québec, if changes are implemented on the Gatineau side but not the Ottawa side; and,
WHEREAS in, light of Manitoba’s recent decision to switch to permanent Daylight Savings Time (DST), the government of Ontario announced on October 13, 2026, that it intends to make daylight saving time permanent in Kenora and the northwestern regions of Ontario that have historically been aligned with neighbouring Manitoba;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council write to the government of Ontario and to local MPPs to encourage them to support the elimination of twice-yearly time changes throughout Ontario, so that the whole province is consistent and aligned with the neighbouring provinces of Manitoba and Québec.

Submitted by Councillor R. Brockington
The provincial Minister of Health, while answering questions from the media recently on why the cost to construct the new Ottawa Hospital located in the Carling/Preston/Prince of Wales vicinity, had increased 5-fold, cited as one of the reasons, increased municipal fees.What are the specific fees the Minister is referring to and what is the total (estimated) sum of those fees?
